differences.title: 1. Query Execution
differences.leftDesc: ClickHouse uses vectorized query execution, processing data in batches (vectors) for high CPU efficiency and cache utilization, optimized for analytical workloads.
differences.rightDesc: StarRocks employs a Massively Parallel Processing (MPP) architecture, distributing query execution across multiple nodes, leveraging row-based and columnar processing.

differences.title: 2. Data Model
differences.leftDesc: ClickHouse excels with denormalized star/snowflake schemas, using MergeTree engines with data skipping indexes for rapid scans and aggregations on large fact tables.
differences.rightDesc: StarRocks supports traditional relational models with foreign keys and joins, optimized for OLAP while maintaining compatibility with transactional query patterns.

differences.title: 3. SQL Dialect
differences.leftDesc: ClickHouse uses a SQL dialect that is powerful for analytics but has its own extensions and functions, requiring adaptation for users familiar with standard SQL.
differences.rightDesc: StarRocks offers high compatibility with MySQL's SQL dialect, simplifying migration and integration for teams already using MySQL-based tools and applications.

differences.title: 4. Data Ingestion
differences.leftDesc: ClickHouse is optimized for large batch inserts and asynchronous merges, providing high throughput but may have higher latency for real-time ingest.
differences.rightDesc: StarRocks supports both batch loading and real-time streaming ingestion pipelines, offering flexibility for diverse data sources and update requirements.

differences.title: 5. Joins
differences.leftDesc: ClickHouse's join performance can be a bottleneck, especially for large fact-to-dimension table joins, often requiring denormalization beforehand.
differences.rightDesc: StarRocks provides robust and efficient join capabilities, including broadcast joins and shuffle joins, crucial for analytical queries on normalized schemas.

differences.title: 6. Architecture
differences.leftDesc: While ClickHouse can be clustered, its core design and optimizations are heavily geared towards single-node performance and efficient columnar storage.
differences.rightDesc: StarRocks is built from the ground up as a distributed OLAP database, designed for horizontal scalability and fault tolerance across multiple compute nodes.

differences.title: 7. Data Updates
differences.leftDesc: ClickHouse's MergeTree engines treat data as largely immutable, with updates/deletes being expensive background operations, making it unsuitable for frequent modifications.
differences.rightDesc: StarRocks supports efficient updates and deletes on its base tables, enabling more dynamic data management and handling of changing analytical requirements.
